items.title: Karnataka schools likely to stay open on Aug 13 as KAMS withdraws bandh closure call
items.summary: Schools across Karnataka are likely to remain open on Thursday, August 13, with the Karnataka Associated Managements of Schools (KAMS) withdrawing its earlier call for school closures. The KAMS had initially called for a closure of schools, as part of a bandh, over the ongoing Cauvery water dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. The KAMS said the decision was taken because another closure would further affect academic schedules, particularly in aided schools already facing a shortage of teachers. KAMS said it would nevertheless extend moral and peaceful support to the bandh called by Kannada organisations to protest Karnataka's release of Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu. School managements, teaching staff and non-teaching employees have been asked to wear black ribbons or black strips as a symbolic gesture, without disrupting classes. The association said academic activities had already been affected because teachers have been deputed for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. items.title: HC can't grant relief if anticipatory bail plea premature: Supreme Court overturns relief to Sunil Biyani
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday set aside a Bombay High Court ruling protecting Future Group’s non-executive director Sunil Biyani from arrest in a ₹1,200-crore Goods and Services Tax (GST) scam [ Union of India v. Sunil Biyani ]. Notably, the High Court had granted this protection even though it held that Biyani's anticipatory bail application in the matter was premature, since the GST authorities had not passed any order under Section 69 (power to arrest) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act. In its February ruling, the High Court had directed that if any such order for Biyani's arrest is issued by the GST authorities, he should not be arrested for a week from the date of intimation of such order. The Central government challenged this ruling before the Supreme Court. It questioned whether High Courts possess inherent jurisdiction to grant interim protection from arrest to a litigant after holding that their anticipatory bail petition is premature and unmaintainable. A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu today ruled that the manner in which protection from arrest was given by the High Court was impermissible. items.title: Tamil Nadu: Engineering student beaten to death; five students held
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A 19-year-old engineering student in Coimbatore was allegedly beaten to death by a group of his college mates on Monday, August 10, following allegations that he was involved in an extortion and mobile phone theft incident. Five students have been detained in connection with the death. The deceased, K Amuthan, was a native of Kallakurichi district, studying at Hindustan Engineering College in Coimbatore. According to reports, Amuthan had recently been suspended from the college hostel after allegedly assaulting a cook employed there. He was subsequently staying with friends in a rented room near Othakkalmandapam. On Monday morning, around 5.30 am, a group of masked youths allegedly entered a rented house in Poonga Nagar, where Elavarasan, 18, a second-year civil engineering student at the same college, was staying with his friends. The group allegedly threatened the occupants with a knife, assaulted them and fled after taking two mobile phones. items.title: Russia appoints former CJI DY Chandrachud as arbitrator in dispute with Ukrainian bank
items.summary: Former Chief Justice of India (CJI) DY Chandrachud has been appointed by Russia as its arbitrator in an investment treaty dispute brought by Ukrainian state-owned bank Oschadbank. According to a report by Global Arbitration Review , Costa Rican arbitrator and former trade minister Dyalá Jiménez will preside over the three-member tribunal. Jiménez was jointly selected as president by both sides. The third arbitrator will be Greek arbitrator and National University of Singapore professor Stavros Brekoulakis who was appointed by Oschadbank. The arbitration has been initiated under the 1998 bilateral investment treaty between Ukraine and Russia. Oschadbank’s claim concerns assets and operations in the Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions that it claims it lost following Russia’s military actions in Ukraine, particularly after the full-scale invasion in 2022. The claim is understood to be worth hundreds of millions of dollars. Oschadbank initiated the proceedings after a notice of dispute served on Russia in July 2025 allegedly went unanswered. items.title: AP junior doctors to stop non-emergency services over pending stipend hike
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Andhra Pradesh Junior Doctors Association (AP JUDA) will discontinue non-emergency services in government medical colleges on Wednesday, August 12, in protest against the Telugu Desam Party (TDP)-led state government. The announcement was made late on Monday, August 11, night after a meeting with the state Health Department. The JUDA said its representatives had met the Andhra Pradesh Director of Medical Education (DME) and other officials to discuss their demands. However, the talks reportedly failed to yield a solution, prompting the doctors to continue their protest. The AP JUDA has been protesting for the implementation of Government Order (GO) 287, issued in 2009. The GO allows for a biannual stipend revision of 15% in view of inflation. The protesters argue that the periodic enhancement of the stipend paid to postgraduate students and interns has been due for more than seven months. The AP JUDA has also demanded that the biannual stipend hike be increased from 15% to 30%, citing rising inflation and workload. The government has instead proposed an annual hike of 3% for postgraduate students and 5% for interns
